about: Case file CF2 (cf2-cost-per-kg-vs-system-cost), wave W2 draft, 2026-11-03. 'timeline' and 'boundary' describe published studies by the course author (Li et al.), drawn from approved excerpts (reports/learn/excerpts_for_approval.md, E3-E5); every study date is the publisher's date on Crossref (accessed 3 Nov 2026). 'idea' is an illustrative toy with invented round numbers (not the studies' inputs or results): an electrolyzer built in 10 MW blocks next to a wind farm, each added block running fewer full-load hours on the wind the grid cannot take. The annual cost per MW, kilograms per MWh and the variable cost are the same stylized values as the allow-listed wind-hydrogen explainer (assets/explainers/wind-hydrogen.js).

boundary.title: Where the journal article's result holds
boundary.lede: The two measures moved apart inside the study's stated boundary:
holds: one planned 253 MW wind farm in West Texas, with ERCOT wholesale prices;
hydrogen sold at a set price per kilogram;
leaves: final federal hydrogen credit rules, which came later;
the rest of the grid, which enters only through wholesale prices;
where the hydrogen goes after it is sold.
boundary.source: From the approved excerpt of Li et al. (2024), Journal of Mechanical Design.

idea.title: Your electrolyzer, one 10 MW block at a time
idea.note: Illustrative numbers, not the studies' inputs or results.
idea.why: Block hours fall because each added block runs only when the surplus wind exceeds the blocks below it. $140,000 per MW-year stands for the electrolyzer's annualized building cost plus fixed upkeep; 18 kg per MWh is about 55 kWh per kg; $0.20 per kg covers water and stack wear. The surplus wind is free because it would otherwise be curtailed.

facts.what: Lower total system cost when an electrolyzer was added, compared with wind and a battery alone (journal case study).
